item.title: REACTION: José Raúl Mulino Wins Panama’s Presidency
item.description: The former security minister and running mate of Ricardo Martinelli won with more than 34% of the vote. Analysts share what this means for Panama’s politics and economy.

item.title: AQ Podcast | Panama: New President, Global Challenges
item.description: Panama sits at the intersection of several big global challenges. In this episode, an overview of what’s ahead for the recently-elected José Raúl Mulino.

item.title: Panama’s New President Signals an Ambitious Agenda
item.description: José Raúl Mulino promises to close the Darién Gap to migration while pushing a major dam to shore up the Panama Canal.

item.title: Panama’s José Raúl Mulino Says He’s “Nobody’s Puppet”
item.description: The president is facing a fiscal crunch, a migration crisis and problems with the Panama Canal. There’s also his powerful political sponsor.

item.title: Panama: A 2025 Snapshot
item.description: AQ tracks political and economic trends to watch and key indicators in 2025.

item.title: Why the U.S. Should Not Take Back the Panama Canal
item.description: There were good reasons to return the canal to Panama. Undoing it now would be a geopolitical disaster.

item.title: What Trump Really Wants in Panama
item.description: Whether it’s countering China, or pursuing a new U.S. expansionism, the president’s threats have already led to concrete action inside Panama, writes AQ’s editor-in-chief.

item.title: AQ Podcast | The Panama Canal: Past, Present and Future
item.description: An overview of Panama’s historical ties to the U.S. and where the crisis might be headed next.

item.title: AQ Podcast | Trump’s Impact So Far on Latin America
item.description: An overview of what Trump’s arrival has meant for Latin America and how governments in the region are reacting to him

item.title: Panama May Need a New Trump Strategy
item.description: The country’s accommodating stance so far hasn’t stopped the U.S. president from demanding the return of the canal.

item.title: Q&A: Panama Canal Authority’s Ricaurte Vásquez Morales
item.description: An interview looking at Trump’s talk, expansion plans—and why Panama might still be the best shipping option, even if the Arctic melts.

item.title: Securing the Panama Canal Requires Diplomacy
item.description: A lighter touch with President Mulino will yield better results for the U.S.

item.title: Panama’s President Mulino Is Right to Cooperate with the U.S.
item.description: Performative resistance to Trump might be gratifying, but it would undermine Panama’s most critical strategic interests, writes Mulino’s former deputy minister of foreign affairs.

item.title: Panama’s Protests Test President Mulino on Multiple Fronts
item.description: Controversial deals with the U.S. have supercharged demonstrations, but the government seems capable of avoiding a repeat of 2023.

item.title: Panama: A 2026 Snapshot
item.description: AQ tracks key indicators and political and economic trends to watch in 2026.
